ground_truth.original_snippet: In order to counterbalance the discussed details, 50% of the pairs will discuss different critical details than the other 50% of the pairs. For example, half the pairs will talk about Eric's cap color but without discussing his company logo (version A of the discussion), while the other pairs will d...

ground_truth.description: Removed item counterbalancing — without it, discussed vs non-discussed comparison confounds item difficulty with experimental manipulation

matched_finding.description: Section 2.3 states that 'discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced,' but Section 2.5 states 'each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.' If all pairs discuss the same four items, discussed/non-discussed status is perfectly confounded with item content. Any differences in accuracy between discussed and non-discussed items could reflect inherent item difficulty differences rather than the effect of misinformation. This undermines the core within-subjects comparison used to measure memory conformity.
matched_finding.quote: In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase. For example, all pairs will talk about Eric's cap color and his company logo.

More precisely, if a pair of participants disagreed with each other and gave d...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s ...
ground_truth.description: Removed disputed/non-disputed classification — treats all discussed items as containing misinformation when some may not have; conflates delivered vs non-delivered misinformation

matched_finding.subcategory: Scoring all discussed items as misinformation regardless of actual content
matched_finding.description: The analysis plan states that all discussed items will be categorized as containing misinformation, even though during actual discussions a partner might provide the correct answer (matching what the participant saw). This mislabeling would introduce noise, attenuate the memory conformity effect, and reduce statistical power. The authors acknowledge this possibility but then contradict it by adopting a blanket categorization approach.
matched_finding.quote: while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner's differing version of events.

ground_truth.modified_snippet: we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation). The main reason for that is that we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take eff...
ground_truth.description: Changed intervention from post- to pre-misinformation — tests encoding prevention instead of retrieval resistance; invalidates IMP theoretical framework which requires post-exposure placement

matched_finding.description: The manuscript contains a direct contradiction about when the experimental interventions are delivered relative to collaborative recall. Section 1.1 states the interventions are placed BEFORE collaborative recall, while the Procedure section (2.5) and Figure 2 description clearly place them AFTER collaborative recall (Phase 3 follows Phase 2). The earlier introduction section also states 'In the present study we decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall,' which contradicts the later claim in Section 1.1. This is a fundamental design ambiguity that makes the study impossible to evaluate or replicate.
matched_finding.quote: What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation).

ground_truth.modified_snippet: Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'non-directional' to 'directional' — reported sample sizes (492, 82, 34) are for two-tailed tests; one-tailed would need smaller N, creating inconsistency

matched_finding.subcategory: Missing alpha level and inference framework
matched_finding.description: The analysis plan does not specify the significance level (alpha), whether one-tailed or two-tailed tests will be used for the main analyses (despite mentioning 'directional significance tests' for power), or whether frequentist, Bayesian, or other inferential frameworks will be applied. These are essential for a registered report.
matched_finding.quote: Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Within-pair age matching removed — must know authority dynamics in memory conformity
ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, the age of the participants in each pair will be matched as far as possible.
ground_truth.description: Removed within-pair age matching — age differences activate authority/deference dynamics that inflate conformity through social influence rather than informational influence

ground_truth.original_snippet: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect has little use in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is little cost of disagreeing (although it is still possible that some pressure exists as the p...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'has little use' to 'completely ruled out' and removed experimenter-awareness caveat — overclaims mechanism specificity

matched_finding.description: The authors claim that normative influence is 'completely ruled out' because the individual memory test involves no interpersonal pressure. However, normative influence can operate during the collaborative recall phase, where participants discuss answers face-to-face. A participant might publicly agree with a partner's answer during discussion due to social pressure, and this public commitment could then influence their subsequent individual responses through cognitive dissonance or commitment-consistency processes. Normative influence at encoding/discussion is not eliminated by an individual test at retrieval.
matched_finding.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Open-ended→forced-choice changes baseline conformity rate and scoring categories — must know format matters
ground_truth.original_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will be in the form of open-ended questions.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.
ground_truth.description: Changed from open-ended to forced-choice — inflates conformity rates (50% guessing baseline vs much lower); scoring categories (correct, misinformation, other) don't make sense with forced-choice

matched_finding.description: The Procedure section describes the individual memory test as containing 20 open-ended questions, while the Analysis Plan section states 'the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.' These are fundamentally different test formats with different scoring properties, different chance performance rates, and different implications for measuring memory conformity. It is unclear which format will actually be used.
matched_finding.quote: The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details included in the movie

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Co-witness exposure exclusion removed — must know non-exposed participants dilute the effect
ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, participants who are not exposed to co-witness details at all (that is, the participants who did not hear any potentially misleading information from the partner) will be excluded from the analyses.
ground_truth.description: Removed exclusion of non-exposed participants — including those who received zero misinformation dilutes the conformity effect and biases against finding both the basic effect and intervention benefit
